customManagers.description: Yarn 1 pinned in Dockerfiles: node:26 images no longer include Yarn, so Dockerfiles install it (RUN command -v yarn >/dev/null || npm install -g yarn@<version>). Renovate keeps that pin current, within Yarn 1 (the org standard; see the yarn rule below)

packageRules.description: Weekly routine group: non-breaking updates move together so lockstep sets cannot split; 0.x patches are non-breaking in practice and automerge. An update whose leading version number changes is kept out (see the cross-major rule below)
npm soak against compromised fresh releases

Docker registries give Renovate no release timestamps, and Renovate 44 treats an update without one as too young forever (minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required), so it never updated a base image (FROM node, dotnet, nginx) and dropped them from branches silently. The age of a Docker tag cannot be measured: let those updates through
0.x minors can break: own branch, dashboard approval, never automerged (regex matcher works for every datasource, unlike isBreaking)
Yarn 1 is the org standard (yarn.lock v1): the Dockerfile pin never leaves 1.x
Major updates need a human: dashboard approval, never automerged

Cross-major guard: Renovate can type a major as minor or patch. A NuGet bare version is a minimum, and when the current release is deprecated Renovate measures from the oldest non-deprecated one (MSTest 3.6.4 -> 4.5.2 was typed 4.5.1 -> 4.5.2, patch). So the leading number of the version actually written decides: if it changes, treat the update as a major
